1 صَرُحَ , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor.
صَرُحَ , (K,) inf. n. صَرَاحَةٌ and صُرُوحَةٌ, (S, O, Msb,) [both strangely said in the K, to be substs.,] It was, or became, pure, sheer, free from admixture, unmingled, unmixed, genuine, or clear; (S, O, Msb, K;) said of a thing (S, O, Msb) of any kind of which the meaning is predicable, (S, O,) [and particularly] said of one's race, or genealogy. (K.) ＝
-A2- صَرَحَ: see 2, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
